# nonObjectLike

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** object-like.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonObjectLike() — Checks whether a value is **not** object-like. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonObjectLike<T>(value: T | object): value is T;
```

`nonObjectLike(value)` is the same test as `!isObjectLike(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

Everything `isObject` accepts, plus functions: the question it answers is whether properties can be read off the value at all.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type          | Description         |
| :-------- | :------------ | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| object` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not object-like; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonObjectLike(null); // => true
nonObjectLike("abc"); // => true
nonObjectLike(1); // => true
nonObjectLike({}); // => false
nonObjectLike([]); // => false
nonObjectLike(function () {}); // => false
```
